title: Subjunctive Anxiety Attack (Trigger Verbs Appear)
style: neurotic jazz rap, 96 BPM, anxious tenor saxophone, double bass walks, brushed snare, dramatic pauses, comedic timing, spoken-word verses, jazz club setting, therapist couch vibe, EN/ES/IT codeswitch, smoky lounge, hooky chorus
lyrics:
[Intro — anxious sax noodle, dramatic pause]
Doctor… I think I have… [pause]
the subjunctive
[sax stab]

[Verse 1 — neurotic spoken-rap, English]
If I were rich — but I'm NOT — that's the tell
Si fuera rico, se fossi ricco, ringing the bell
Reality versus possibility splits the verb
Indicative is what IS, subjunctive's the disturbed

[Pre-Chorus — therapy couch confessional]
I wish you would call me — ojalá me llamaras
Magari mi chiamassi — three languages, same trauma
Doubt and desire, hope and fear, command
Trigger verbs appear, trigger verbs at hand!

[Chorus — full anxious jazz freakout]
The subjunctive is when you're not SURE
Doubt and desire, hope and FEAR
WANT, REQUEST, DENY, FEEL — they pull the trigger near
The subjunctive anxiety is HERE, HERE, HERE!

[Verse 2 — rapid-fire, all three]
"Quiero que vengas" — I want you to come, but I can't make you
"Voglio che tu venga" — Italian wants the same thing too
"It is important that he BE on time" — yes BE, not IS
English barely uses it, the rest of us live IN it!

[Verse 3 — therapy session]
My therapist says "I hope you feel better soon"
She used the SUBJUNCTIVE — feel, not feels, in tune
The trigger verb HOPE pulled the mood right out
I'm CURED, doctor, I figured it OUT!

[Bridge — slow, contemplative sax]
If I had known, si hubiera sabido, se avessi saputo
Past subjunctive, the regrets we live through
Conditional sentences, third type, the unreal
The grammar of grief is what these verbs reveal

[Final Chorus]
The subjunctive is when you're not SURE
Doubt and desire, hope and FEAR
WANT, REQUEST, DENY, FEEL — they pull the trigger near
The subjunctive anxiety is HERE, HERE, HERE!

[Outro — whispered]
Ojalá. Magari. If only.
